sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenBB's Open Data Platform (ODP) is an open-source Python toolkit for pulling financial and other data from many providers through one interface. You can use it in Python, as a command-line tool, or as a local API that feeds dashboards, Excel, AI copilots and the OpenBB Workspace.
sixtySeconds.problem: Financial data lives in many separate APIs, each with its own format. ODP lets you connect data sources once and use them everywhere, for example getting a stock's price history as a pandas DataFrame in one line.
whoFor: Quants and analysts working in Python
OpenBB Workspace users adding their own data
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, Apache-2.0 data layer with many integrations and a ready API server. The README warns that data is not necessarily accurate and trading carries high risk.
requirements: API keys for any paid data providers you connect

overview: ODP is described as connect-once, consume-everywhere infrastructure. In Python, from openbb import obb gives you commands such as obb.equity.price.historical("AAPL"), and results convert to DataFrames.

Running openbb-api starts a FastAPI server on 127.0.0.1:6900, which you can connect to OpenBB Workspace (the company's enterprise UI for analysts and AI agents) under Apps, then Connect backend. A separate ODP CLI installs with pip install openbb-cli.

The project includes many data integrations, listed in its documentation. The README's disclaimer says trading involves high risk, the data is not necessarily accurate, and OpenBB accepts no liability for losses from relying on it.

steps.title: Fetch data
steps.code:
from openbb import obb
output = obb.equity.price.historical("AAPL")
df = output.to_dataframe()

firstRun.title: Get Apple's price history in Python
firstRun.code:
from openbb import obb
df = obb.equity.price.historical("AAPL").to_dataframe()
print(df.tail())

tutorial.title: Connect your own data backend to OpenBB Workspace
tutorial.useCase: Serve ODP locally and use it from the Workspace UI.

steps.title: Open OpenBB Workspace
steps.body: Go to the Apps tab and click Connect backend.

steps.title: Add the backend
steps.body: Name it Open Data Platform, use URL http://127.0.0.1:6900, click Test, then Add.

tutorial.expected: Workspace reports a successful test with the number of apps found, and your ODP data appears in Workspace.
